title: Admin - Content Management - Create New Informational Page - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Content Management - Create New Informational Page feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Admins to create new informational pages via a modal with Title and Content fields, auto-generated slug from the title, and save options (Draft or Published). The new page appears in the page list after saving. Covers happy path, form validation, slug generation, save states, and error handling.

testCases.title: Clicking Add Article opens the page creation modal
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Content Management page is loaded.
expectedResults: The 'Add Article' button is visible on the Content Management page
Clicking the button opens a page creation modal/dialog
The modal contains fields for Page Title and Page Content
The modal has Save as Draft and Publish buttons
The modal has a way to close/cancel
testCases.postconditions: Page creation modal is open and ready for input

testCases.title: Admin can enter Page Title
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Locate the Page Title input field
Type a title (e.g., 'Getting Started with Assistive Technology')
expectedResults: A Page Title input field is present and visible
The field accepts text input
The typed title appears in the field
The field has a label or placeholder indicating its purpose
testCases.postconditions: Page Title field contains the entered text

testCases.title: Admin can enter Page Content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Locate the Page Content field (text area or rich text editor)
Enter content text (e.g., 'This page provides information about assistive technology products available on our platform.')
expectedResults: A Page Content field is present (textarea or rich text editor)
The field accepts text input
The entered content is displayed in the field
The field supports multi-line text
testCases.postconditions: Page Content field contains the entered text

testCases.title: System auto-generates slug from the title
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Enter a title: 'Getting Started with Assistive Technology'
Observe the slug field or slug preview
expectedResults: A slug is automatically generated from the title
The slug is in URL-friendly format (lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces)
Example: 'getting-started-with-assistive-technology'
The slug updates as the title changes
Special characters are removed or replaced in the slug
testCases.postconditions: Slug is auto-generated and matches the title

testCases.title: Admin can save page as Draft
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open with title and content filled.
expectedResults: The page is saved successfully as a Draft
A success notification may be displayed
The modal closes after saving
The page appears in the page list with 'Draft' status
The page is NOT publicly visible (draft only)
testCases.postconditions: Page is saved as Draft and visible in the page list

testCases.title: Admin can save page as Published
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open with title and content filled.
expectedResults: The page is saved and published successfully
A success notification may be displayed
The modal closes after publishing
The page appears in the page list with 'Published' status
The page is publicly accessible via its slug URL
testCases.postconditions: Page is published and visible in the page list

testCases.title: Page appears in page list after saving
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page has just been created (Draft or Published).
steps: Create a new page with title and content
Save the page (as Draft or Published)
After modal closes, observe the page list
Verify the new page is present
expectedResults: The page list updates immediately without page refresh
The new page is visible in the list
The page shows the correct title
The page shows the correct status (Draft or Published)
The page shows the auto-generated slug
testCases.postconditions: New page is confirmed in the page list

testCases.title: Empty title field shows validation error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Leave the Page Title field empty
expectedResults: The form does NOT submit
A validation error is displayed for the Title field (e.g., 'Title is required')
The modal remains open for correction
No page is created in the list
testCases.postconditions: Empty title is rejected with validation error

testCases.title: Empty content field shows validation error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Leave the Page Content field empty
expectedResults: The form does NOT submit
A validation error is displayed for the Content field (e.g., 'Content is required')
The modal remains open for correction
No page is created in the list
testCases.postconditions: Empty content is rejected with validation error

testCases.title: Duplicate slug shows error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A page with slug 'getting-started' already exists.
steps: Enter a title that would generate a duplicate slug (e.g., 'Getting Started')
expectedResults: The system detects the duplicate slug
An error message is displayed (e.g., 'A page with this URL already exists')
The modal remains open for the user to modify the title
OR the system auto-appends a number to make the slug unique (e.g., 'getting-started-2')
No duplicate page is created

testCases.title: API failure during save shows error notification
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open. API is configured to fail.
expectedResults: An error notification is displayed (e.g., 'Failed to save page. Please try again.')
The modal remains open so the user can retry
No partial/corrupt page is created
The user can attempt to save again

testCases.title: Slug generation handles special characters correctly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Enter a title with special characters: 'FAQ's & Tips: Getting Started!'
expectedResults: Special characters are removed or replaced (apostrophes, ampersands, colons, exclamation marks)
The slug is URL-safe (e.g., 'faqs-tips-getting-started')
No invalid URL characters remain in the slug
The slug is readable and meaningful

testCases.title: Modal can be closed without saving
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open with data entered.
steps: Enter title and content in the modal
Close the modal without saving (click X, press Escape, or click Cancel)
expectedResults: The modal closes without saving
No new page is created in the list
No error messages are shown
The entered data is discarded
testCases.postconditions: No page is created when modal is closed without saving

testCases.title: Title field accepts various character types
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Enter a title with alphabetic characters
Enter a title with Unicode/special characters
Enter a very long title (100+ characters)
expectedResults: Alphabetic titles are accepted
Titles with numbers are accepted
Unicode characters are handled (accepted or sanitized)
Long titles are either accepted or truncated with clear feedback
The field does not crash with any input
testCases.postconditions: Title field handles various inputs correctly

testCases.title: Content field supports rich text or multi-line input
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Page creation modal is open.
steps: Enter content with formatting (if rich text editor is available)
Enter a large amount of content (1000+ characters)
expectedResults: Multi-line content is preserved
If rich text: formatting options work (bold, italic, links, etc.)
Large content is accepted without truncation
The content field scrolls or expands for long content
testCases.postconditions: Content field supports expected input types
